use: Identifies the standing fortress, the 1783 reconstruction, five masonry corners, moat, and operation as the historical museum.
Official facsimile of the successor fort scheme with the public entrance axis and open center.
Official facsimile of Panón’s 1779 construction survey of the masonry and dry moat.
Independent museum-archive citation for Panón’s plan and folio number.
The national historical monuments record describes coursed stone and partial render, a fixed masonry bridge and a neoclassical arched entrance with Tuscan pilasters and a triangular pediment.
